transcript: Okay, when everything is urgent. So in sales that's, like, every Monday, haha. What I usually do is, I look at my pipeline first thing and I check which deals are closest to closing, because those are the ones where if I'm slow, I can actually lose money. Those go first. Then renewals, because keeping a client is easier than finding a new one. And then prospecting, new leads, that kind of comes last in the day. For example, one week I had a proposal due for a mid-size retailer, a renewal call with an existing client who was unhappy about pricing, and my manager wanted the forecast updated. I did the proposal in the morning, the renewal call after lunch, and I did the forecast in the evening, a bit late, my manager wasn't super happy about that. Sometimes I don't tell people early enough that their thing is going to wait. That's something I'm working on. But yeah, generally closest to money first, then keeping existing clients, then the rest. It works most of the time for me, I'd say.
